articles.summary: Maharashtra CM Meets Nandan Nilekani Panel, Discusses Measures to Make NTA Exams Secure Jagran Josh
articles.content: The Maharashtra government is considering a bigger role in conducting national-level examinations organised by the National Testing Agency (NTA) to improve examination security, transparency and accessibility. The proposal was discussed during a meeting between Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and the Centre-appointed High-Powered Task Force on Examination Reforms, chaired by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani.The meeting was held on November 23 at the Chief Minister’s official residence, Varsha, in Mumbai. The discussions focused on strengthening coordination between the state government and central examination agencies to ensure that national-level entrance examinations are conducted smoothly and securely.According to an official government release, Maharashtra wants to make better use of its existing infrastructure for conducting examinations. The state also highlighted the need to ensure adequate examination centres in every district, provide necessary facilities and train personnel deployed at these centres.The discussions also covered the logistical arrangements required to conduct large-scale examinations and establish a secure environment for candidates. The objective is to prevent examination malpractices and maintain the credibility of national-level tests.NTA Exam Reforms: Focus on Accessibility and Student ConvenienceThe meeting also discussed ways to provide equal examination opportunities to students from rural and urban areas. Participants highlighted the need to make examinations more accessible to candidates who face difficulties with the English language and students with disabilities.Another important issue was reducing examination-related stress. The participants discussed providing students with more opportunities to appear for examinations and deciding examination patterns according to the nature of the syllabus.The need to offer guidance and training facilities to students preparing for competitive and entrance examinations was also discussed.Who Attended the Meeting?Apart from Devendra Fadnavis and Nandan Nilekani, the meeting was attended by former ISRO chairman Dr S Somanath, Shankar Maruwada and National Recruitment Agency (NRA) Director Shruti Singhal, among other officials.The task force was constituted by the Centre in July 2026 to examine and recommend comprehensive reforms in the conduct, security, design and governance of public examinations, including those organised by the NTA.The panel is examining measures to address concerns over examination irregularities and paper leaks and strengthen the overall examination system.The discussions with Maharashtra are part of the wider consultation process to improve the conduct of national-level examinations. However, no final decision on giving Maharashtra additional responsibility in conducting NTA examinations has been announced so far. articles.contentHindi: महाराष्ट्र सरकार परीक्षा सुरक्षा, पारदर्शिता और पहुंच में सुधार के लिए राष्ट्रीय परीक्षण एजेंसी (एनटीए) द्वारा आयोजित राष्ट्रीय स्तर की परीक्षाओं के संचालन में एक बड़ी भूमिका पर विचार कर रही है। इस प्रस्ताव पर इंफोसिस के सह-संस्थापक नंदन नीलेकणि की अध्यक्षता में मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फड़नवीस और परीक्षा सुधार पर केंद्र द्वारा नियुक्त उच्चाधिकार प्राप्त टास्क फोर्स के बीच एक बैठक के दौरान चर्चा की गई। बैठक 23 नवंबर को मुंबई में मुख्यमंत्री के आधिकारिक निवास, वर्षा में आयोजित की गई थी। चर्चा राज्य सरकार और केंद्रीय परीक्षा एजेंसियों के बीच समन्वय को मजबूत करने पर केंद्रित थी ताकि यह सुनिश्चित किया जा सके कि राष्ट्रीय स्तर की प्रवेश परीक्षाएं सुचारू और सुरक्षित रूप से आयोजित की जाएं। एक आधिकारिक सरकारी विज्ञप्ति के अनुसार, महाराष्ट्र परीक्षा आयोजित करने के लिए अपने मौजूदा बुनियादी ढांचे का बेहतर उपयोग करना चाहता है। राज्य ने हर जिले में पर्याप्त परीक्षा केंद्र सुनिश्चित करने, आवश्यक सुविधाएं प्रदान करने और इन केंद्रों पर तैनात कर्मियों को प्रशिक्षित करने की आवश्यकता पर भी प्रकाश डाला। चर्चा में बड़े पैमाने पर परीक्षा आयोजित करने और उम्मीदवारों के लिए एक सुरक्षित वातावरण स्थापित करने के लिए आवश्यक तार्किक व्यवस्था पर भी चर्चा हुई। इसका उद्देश्य परीक्षा में गड़बड़ी को रोकना और राष्ट्रीय स्तर की परीक्षाओं की विश्वसनीयता बनाए रखना है। एनटीए परीक्षा सुधार: पहुंच और छात्र सुविधा पर ध्यान देंबैठक में ग्रामीण और शहरी क्षेत्रों के छात्रों को समान परीक्षा के अवसर प्रदान करने के तरीकों पर भी चर्चा हुई। प्रतिभागियों ने अंग्रेजी भाषा में कठिनाइयों का सामना करने वाले उम्मीदवारों और विकलांग छात्रों के लिए परीक्षाओं को अधिक सुलभ बनाने की आवश्यकता पर प्रकाश डाला। एक अन्य महत्वपूर्ण मुद्दा परीक्षा से संबंधित तनाव को कम करना था। प्रतिभागियों ने छात्रों को परीक्षाओं में बैठने के अधिक अवसर प्रदान करने और पाठ्यक्रम की प्रकृति के अनुसार परीक्षा पैटर्न तय करने पर चर्चा की। प्रतिस्पर्धी और प्रवेश परीक्षाओं की तैयारी करने वाले छात्रों को मार्गदर्शन और प्रशिक्षण सुविधाएं प्रदान करने की आवश्यकता पर भी चर्चा की गई। बैठक में किसने भाग लिया? बैठक में देवेंद्र फड़नवीस और नंदन नीलेकणि के अलावा, इसरो के पूर्व अध्यक्ष डॉ एस सोमनाथ, शंकर मारुवाड़ा और राष्ट्रीय भर्ती एजेंसी (एनआरए) के निदेशक श्रुति सिंघल सहित अन्य अधिकारी शामिल थे। केंद्र द्वारा जुलाई 2026 में जांच और सिफारिश करने के लिए टास्क फोर्स का गठन किया गया था। एनटीए द्वारा आयोजित परीक्षाओं सहित सार्वजनिक परीक्षाओं के संचालन, सुरक्षा, डिजाइन और प्रशासन में व्यापक सुधार। पैनल परीक्षा अनियमितताओं और पेपर लीक पर चिंताओं को दूर करने और समग्र परीक्षा प्रणाली को मजबूत करने के उपायों की जांच कर रहा है। महाराष्ट्र के साथ चर्चा राष्ट्रीय स्तर की परीक्षाओं के संचालन में सुधार के लिए व्यापक परामर्श प्रक्रिया का हिस्सा है। हालाँकि, एनटीए परीक्षा आयोजित करने में महाराष्ट्र को अतिरिक्त जिम्मेदारी देने पर अभी तक कोई अंतिम निर्णय घोषित नहीं किया गया है। यह भी पढ़ें| राष्ट्रीय परीक्षा 2026: संसदीय पैनल एनटीए सुधारों, परीक्षा पेपर लीक संबंधी चिंताओं की समीक्षा करेगा। यह भी पढ़ें| एनटीए ने 4-दिवसीय चिंतन शिविर की मेजबानी की: परीक्षा की शुचिता बढ़ाने और उम्मीदवार का आत्मविश्वास बहाल करने के लिए प्रमुख सुधार पेश किए गए

articles.contentMarathi: परीक्षा सुरक्षा, पारदर्शकता आणि सुलभता सुधारण्यासाठी नॅशनल टेस्टिंग एजन्सी (NTA) द्वारे आयोजित राष्ट्रीय स्तरावरील परीक्षा आयोजित करण्यात महाराष्ट्र सरकार मोठ्या भूमिकेचा विचार करत आहे. मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस आणि इन्फोसिसचे सह-संस्थापक नंदन निलेकणी यांच्या अध्यक्षतेखाली परीक्षा सुधारणांबाबत केंद्र-नियुक्त उच्चाधिकार टास्क फोर्स यांच्यात झालेल्या बैठकीत या प्रस्तावावर चर्चा करण्यात आली. 23 नोव्हेंबर रोजी मुंबईतील मुख्यमंत्र्यांच्या शासकीय निवासस्थानी वर्षा येथे ही बैठक झाली. राष्ट्रीय स्तरावरील प्रवेश परीक्षा सुरळीतपणे आणि सुरक्षितपणे पार पाडल्या जाव्यात यासाठी राज्य सरकार आणि केंद्रीय परीक्षा संस्था यांच्यातील समन्वय मजबूत करण्यावर या चर्चेत भर देण्यात आला. अधिकृत सरकारी प्रकाशनानुसार, परीक्षा आयोजित करण्यासाठी महाराष्ट्राला सध्याच्या पायाभूत सुविधांचा अधिक चांगला वापर करायचा आहे. राज्याने प्रत्येक जिल्ह्यात पुरेशी परीक्षा केंद्रे सुनिश्चित करण्याची, आवश्यक सुविधा उपलब्ध करून देण्याची आणि या केंद्रांवर तैनात कर्मचाऱ्यांना प्रशिक्षित करण्याची गरज अधोरेखित केली. मोठ्या प्रमाणावर परीक्षा आयोजित करण्यासाठी आणि उमेदवारांसाठी सुरक्षित वातावरण निर्माण करण्यासाठी आवश्यक असलेल्या लॉजिस्टिक व्यवस्थेचाही या चर्चेत समावेश करण्यात आला. परीक्षेतील गैरप्रकारांना आळा घालणे आणि राष्ट्रीय स्तरावरील चाचण्यांची विश्वासार्हता राखणे हा यामागचा उद्देश आहे. NTA परीक्षा सुधारणा: प्रवेशक्षमता आणि विद्यार्थ्यांच्या सोयीवर लक्ष केंद्रित कराया बैठकीत ग्रामीण आणि शहरी भागातील विद्यार्थ्यांना समान परीक्षा संधी उपलब्ध करून देण्याच्या मार्गांवर चर्चा करण्यात आली. सहभागींनी इंग्रजी भाषेच्या अडचणींचा सामना करणाऱ्या उमेदवारांसाठी आणि अपंग विद्यार्थ्यांना परीक्षा अधिक सुलभ बनविण्याची गरज अधोरेखित केली. परीक्षा संबंधित ताण कमी करणे हा आणखी एक महत्त्वाचा मुद्दा होता. सहभागींनी विद्यार्थ्यांना परीक्षेला बसण्यासाठी अधिक संधी उपलब्ध करून देणे आणि अभ्यासक्रमाच्या स्वरूपानुसार परीक्षा पद्धती ठरवणे यावर चर्चा केली. स्पर्धात्मक आणि प्रवेश परीक्षांची तयारी करणाऱ्या विद्यार्थ्यांना मार्गदर्शन आणि प्रशिक्षण सुविधा देण्याची गरज यावरही चर्चा करण्यात आली. बैठकीला कोण कोण उपस्थित होते? देवेंद्र फडणवीस आणि नंदन निलेकणी यांच्या व्यतिरिक्त, आयएसआरओचे माजी अध्यक्ष एस.आर.ओ.चे राष्ट्रीय अध्यक्ष डॉ. शंकरराव, डॉ. रिक्रूटमेंट एजन्सी (NRA) च्या संचालक श्रुती सिंघल, इतर अधिकाऱ्यांसह. केंद्राने जुलै 2026 मध्ये NTA द्वारे आयोजित केलेल्या परीक्षांचे आचरण, सुरक्षा, रचना आणि प्रशासनामध्ये सर्वसमावेशक सुधारणा तपासण्यासाठी आणि शिफारस करण्यासाठी टास्क फोर्सची स्थापना करण्यात आली होती. हे पॅनेल महाराष्ट्राच्या परीक्षेतील अनियमितता आणि परीक्षांच्या अनियमिततेबद्दलच्या चिंता दूर करण्यासाठी उपायांचे परीक्षण करत आहे. राष्ट्रीय स्तरावरील परीक्षांचे आयोजन सुधारण्यासाठी व्यापक सल्लामसलत प्रक्रिया. तथापि, NTA परीक्षा आयोजित करण्यासाठी महाराष्ट्राला अतिरिक्त जबाबदारी देण्याचा कोणताही अंतिम निर्णय अद्याप जाहीर झालेला नाही. हे देखील वाचा| राष्ट्रीय परीक्षा 2026: NTA सुधारणांचे पुनरावलोकन करण्यासाठी संसदीय पॅनेल, परीक्षा पेपर लीकच्या संदर्भातही वाचा| NTA 4-दिवसीय चिंतन शिविर आयोजित करतो: परीक्षेची अखंडता वाढवण्यासाठी आणि उमेदवाराचा आत्मविश्वास पुनर्संचयित करण्यासाठी मुख्य सुधारणा सादर केल्या आहेत

articles.title: Priyansh Arya unleashes carnage, smashes 181 to set new Indian T20 record - India Today
articles.summary: Priyansh Arya unleashes carnage, smashes 181 to set new Indian T20 record India Today
articles.content: Priyansh Arya produced a breathtaking batting display in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy on Tuesday, smashing 181 off just 68 balls to script history against Tamil Nadu in Indore.The Delhi captain became the highest individual scorer by an Indian in T20 cricket and registered the second-highest individual score in men's T20 history. His extraordinary innings also saw him equal the record for the most sixes in a men's T20 innings.Arya's assault was built around 19 sixes and seven fours, with the left-handed opener scoring at a strike rate of 266.17. He fell just seven runs short of the world record of 188 not out, held by South Africa's Lhuan-dre Gilbert Pretorius, who achieved the feat in the CSA Pro20 Cup last month.The 25-year-old's remarkable contribution powered Delhi to 275 for five, equalling the joint third-highest total in Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy history.ARYA TOPS INDIAN RECORDSArya's 181 took him past several established records in Indian cricket. His innings eclipsed Kiran Navgire's 162 off 76 balls, scored in the Women's Senior T20 Trophy in 2021, to become the highest individual score by an Indian in T20 cricket.He also moved past KL Rahul's record for the highest individual score by an Indian in men's T20 cricket. Rahul had scored an unbeaten 152 off 67 balls for Delhi Capitals against Punjab Kings in April this year.The Delhi captain also surpassed Tilak Varma's previous Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy record of 151 not out against Meghalaya in November 2024.Arya's 181 is now the highest individual score in the tournament's history.JOINS FINN ALLENArya's 19 sixes were another major highlight of an innings dominated by clean hitting and relentless aggression.He equalled New Zealand batter Finn Allen's record for the most sixes in a men's T20 innings. Allen had struck 19 sixes for San Francisco Unicorns against Washington Freedom in Major League Cricket in June 2025.Arya also became the highest-scoring Indian captain in men's T20 cricket, adding another record to an already extraordinary day.SEVEN SHORT OF WORLD RECORDWhile Arya could not quite reach the overall T20 world record, he came remarkably close.Pretorius holds the record with his unbeaten 188 off 79 balls against the Knights in October 2026. Arya's 181 is now second on the all-time list of highest individual scores in men's T20 cricket.Chris Gayle's unbeaten 175 off 66 balls for Royal Challengers Bangalore against Pune Warriors India in 2013 remains third on the list, followed by Aaron Finch's 172 off 76 balls for Australia against Zimbabwe in 2018.PRIYANSH ARYA'S RECORDSMOST SIXES IN A MEN'S T20 INNINGSFinn Allen – 19 sixes (151 off 51 balls)Priyansh Arya – 19 sixes (181 off 68 balls)Chris Gayle – 18 sixes (146* off 69 balls)Sahil Chauhan – 18 sixes (144* off 41 balls)Chris Gayle – 17 sixes (175* off 66 balls)Prashant Bisht – 17 sixes (146* off 51 balls)HIGHEST INDIVIDUAL SCORES IN SMAT HISTORYPriyansh Arya – 181 off 68 balls vs Tamil Nadu (2026)Tilak Varma – 151 off 67 balls vs Meghalaya (2024)Abhishek Sharma – 148 off 52 balls vs Bengal (2025)Shreyas Iyer – 147 off 55 balls vs Sikkim (2019)Prashant Bisht – 146* off 51 balls vs Mizoram (2021)HIGHEST INDIVIDUAL SCORES IN MEN'S T20 CRICKETLhuan-dre Pretorius – 188* off 79 balls vs Knights (2026)Priyansh Arya – 181 off 68 balls vs Tamil Nadu (2026)Chris Gayle – 175* off 66 balls vs Pune Warriors (2013)Aaron Finch – 172 off 76 balls vs Zimbabwe (2018)Hamza Khan – 164* off 65 balls vs Ivory Coast (2026)HIGHEST INDIVIDUAL SCORES BY CAPTAINS IN MEN'S T20 CRICKETPriyansh Arya – 181 off 68 balls vs Tamil Nadu (2026)Aaron Finch – 172 off 76 balls vs Zimbabwe (2018)Karanbir Singh – 164 off 57 balls vs Hungary (2026)Glenn Maxwell – 154* off 64 balls vs Hurricanes (2022)Tilak Varma – 151 off 67 balls vs Meghalaya (2024)- Ends

articles.summary: IFFI 2026: Maharashtra Government plans new push for global film collaborations and independent cinema – MovieTalkies
articles.content: IFFI 2026 Maharashtra Government Global Push For Low Budget Cinema: The Maharashtra government is planning to introduce a dedicated mechanism to encourage international film co-productions and help independent films reach wider audiences. The proposed initiatives aim to strengthen the state's film ecosystem and make Maharashtra a more attractive destination for domestic as well as international filmmakers. Sara Tendulkar and Rajveer Deol getting married? Here's the truth – The plans were discussed by Dr. Kiran Kulkarni, Secretary of the Cultural Affairs Department, Government of Maharashtra, during a panel discussion at the 57th International Film Festival of India – IFFI 2026 – in Goa today. Organised by the Maharashtra Film, Stage and Cultural Development Corporation at the Waves Film Bazaar , the session focused on the future opportunities and growth of Maharashtra's cultural and film industries. The panel included filmmaker Nikhil Mahajan, cinematographer-director Mahesh Limaye , filmmaker-producer Suhrud Godbole and Prashant Sajanikar, Joint Managing Director of the Corporation. Film scholar and director Dr. Santosh Pathare moderated the discussion. During the session, Kulkarni said the state government would work towards setting up an institutional framework through the Corporation to make international film collaborations easier. The proposal came after Nikhil Mahajan pointed out the increasing interest among foreign production houses in working with Indian filmmakers. A structured mechanism could help Marathi and other Indian-language films find international partners, explore new markets and build cross-border creative collaborations. Kulkarni also highlighted Maharashtra's single-window clearance system for film shoots, which aims to provide permissions from different government departments within seven days. Around 5,000 permissions for outdoor shooting locations have already been issued through this system, making it easier for production houses to shoot across the state. Another important subject discussed was the difficulty faced by independent filmmakers in securing theatrical releases. High multiplex ticket prices, limited screenings and inconvenient show timings often restrict the reach of smaller films. Kulkarni said the government was exploring technology-based solutions to improve theatrical access and help low-budget films connect with more viewers. Discussions with the concerned departments are also underway. Prashant Sajanikar stressed that developing a strong film ecosystem requires more than infrastructure, adding that the Corporation is engaging with filmmakers to understand their changing requirements and address industry challenges. Mahesh Limaye highlighted Maharashtra's diverse shooting locations and production facilities while emphasising the importance of maintaining them responsibly. He urged production teams to restore locations after shoots so that other filmmakers could continue using them. Meanwhile, Suhrud Godbole welcomed efforts to take emerging Marathi filmmakers to international festivals such as Cannes . He noted that global exposure can help young directors develop professional connections, understand international filmmaking practices and explore future collaborations. articles.summary: Indian sports wrap, November 23: Top BGMI players to battle for Solo Legend title at Museo Camera in December Sportstar
articles.content: CHENNAI ESPORTS BGMI LAN finale at Gurugram museum on December 3 India’s top Battlegrounds Mobile India (BGMI) players will compete for the title of the country’s next Solo Legend on December 3, as Red Bull Solo Legends - Season 2 culminates in a LAN Finale at Museo Camera Centre for the Photographic Arts in Gurugram. Unlike conventional BGMI esports competitions, which are built around four-player squads, Red Bull Solo Legends puts individual ability at the centre of the action. Every engagement, rotation and survival decision rests with the player, making it a test of mechanics, strategy and composure without the support of teammates. The LAN Finale will feature 56 players, comprising 28 qualifiers from the Pro Qualifiers, 12 from the Open Qualifiers, four college winners, four directly invited professionals and eight Chaos Agents. The winner will be determined by a points-based system that rewards kills and placement, with additional points for eliminating Chaos Agents. The player with the highest cumulative score will be crowned as the champion and receive a complete gaming room makeover from Red Bull. The tournament’s Rising Star, selected from the Open and College Qualifiers, will receive a two-day experience at the bootcamp of GodLike Esports, one of India’s leading esports organisations, including mentorship and an opportunity to spend time alongside its professional athletes. The Open Qualifiers, which concluded earlier this month, attracted more than 13,000 participants, with players progressing through multiple online rounds to secure their place in the competition. The four-day Pro Qualifiers will take place from November 23 to 26, with 84 professional players competing for 28 places at the finale. The eight Chaos Agents are invited veterans from the BGMI community, who will bring an added challenge to the finalists, with bonus points up for grabs for players who eliminate them. Last season’s winner Harsh Malik (Spraygod), Red Bull player Jonathan Amaral (Jonathan Gaming), Rudra Banswani (Spower), and Mohammed Lakhani (Owais) constitute this group. “What makes Red Bull Solo Legends exciting is that it takes away the safety net of playing in a team. You have to rely entirely on your own game sense, decision-making and mechanics, and every player gets an opportunity to prove themselves on the same stage,” said Jonathan. articles.contentHindi: CHENNAI ESPORTS BGMI LAN finale at Gurugram museum on December 3 India’s top Battlegrounds Mobile India (BGMI) players will compete for the title of the country’s next Solo Legend on December 3, as Red Bull Solo Legends - Season 2 culminates in a LAN Finale at Museo Camera Centre for the Photographic Arts in Gurugram. Unlike conventional BGMI esports competitions, which are built around four-player squads, Red Bull Solo Legends puts individual ability at the centre of the action. Every engagement, rotation and survival decision rests with the player, making it a test of mechanics, strategy and composure without the support of teammates. The LAN Finale will feature 56 players, comprising 28 qualifiers from the Pro Qualifiers, 12 from the Open Qualifiers, four college winners, four directly invited professionals and eight Chaos Agents. The winner will be determined by a points-based system that rewards kills and placement, with additional points for eliminating Chaos Agents. The player with the highest cumulative score will be crowned as the champion and receive a complete gaming room makeover from Red Bull. The tournament’s Rising Star, selected from the Open and College Qualifiers, will receive a two-day experience at the bootcamp of GodLike Esports, one of India’s leading esports organisations, including mentorship and an opportunity to spend time alongside its professional athletes.
